Two candidates I'd benchmark: have workers draft tests for separate modules with fixed interfaces, or investigate independent bug reports and return repro steps plus likely files. Keep final review/integration on the 5090. Avoid having workers edit the same files.



Run the same small batch sequentially, then with two concurrent workers. Compare total time to accepted results, including review and retries. That tests whether the second machine adds useful capacity; it doesn't assume the smaller model will be faster overall.



Hermes documents parallel independent workstreams here: [https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/delegation-patterns](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/delegation-patterns)

Could you share a couple of concrete workflow examples where parallel subagent execution genuinely beats a single model pipeline in throughput and efficiency?

Main model + 3 subagents, each with different perspectives, research the same topic -> main agent assesses and aggregates all four analyses and combines into one report based on subagent consensus + main model judgment.

Do you mean that you add specialised bots?

  
Different employees are analyzing the same topic and presenting their findings—hmm, that’s a different and interesting approach. ty for response.

No not specialized bots. I just have the main agent delegate the same task to three spontaneous subagents, but each with a slightly different prompt to have them do the task in a different way. When all agents finish their tasks, the main agent then acts as a judge to cherry pick the best work produced. This can be done on a single profile, and works better than trying to work with Kanban.
